mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months compresses equity discount rates and increases risk appetite, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months, it signals restrictive monetary policy that increases equity discount rates and reduces corporate borrowing, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for 2 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicate weakening consumer demand and labor market stress, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint condition of HOUST decline and UNRATE rise fails to predict negative returns in more than 60% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansions with GDPC1 annual growth exceeding 3.0%, overvaluation and profit-taking pressures cause negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: In periods where GDPC1 annual growth exceeds 3.0%, 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate trend over the past 3 months signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE rises for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 5.0% for two consecutive months, it indicates severe labor market weakness that depresses equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0% for 2 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and rise in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) indicate stagflationary pressures that reduce corporate profit margins and increase risk aversion, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: The joint condition of INDPRO decline and CPIAUCSL rise fails to predict negative returns in more than 60% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During supply chain recovery phases marked by INDPRO growth above 1.5% monthly, expanding production capacity accelerates earnings growth, yielding positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: In periods where INDPRO monthly growth exceeds 1.5%, 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of cases.
